It is **not a prescriptive deployment guide** and does not mandate specific products, vendors, or UEM platforms. Actual Solution Building Block selection and implementation occur in TOGAF ADM Phases E–F. This document defines architectural patterns and integration requirements only.

[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-UEM-RAD-3.4.03.md#purpose]

### Purpose

This Reference Architecture defines the architectural pattern for managing the full enterprise endpoint estate — workstations, laptops, mobile devices, virtual desktops, and servers — through a unified management architecture that provides a single operational plane for asset inventory, configuration policy deployment, compliance monitoring, and security baseline enforcement across all device populations regardless of form factor or network location.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-UEM-RAD-3.4.03.md#scope]

### Scope

This Reference Architecture covers:
- Unified device enrollment and registration across device populations
- Policy management: configuration baseline deployment to heterogeneous device populations
- Compliance monitoring and reporting across corporate, mobile, and BYOD device populations
- Security agent deployment orchestration through the UEM management plane
- Certificate provisioning for managed device identity
- Integration between UEM and asset inventory as the authoritative device registry

[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-UEM-RAD-3.4.03.md#device-population-coverage-model]

### Device Population Coverage Model

| Device Population | Enrollment Mechanism | Configuration Delivery | Compliance Signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Corporate workstations (domain-joined) | Domain enrollment + management agent | Group Policy / Management agent | Management agent compliance report |
| Corporate laptops (cloud-joined) | Cloud management enrollment + management agent | Cloud policy / Management agent | Cloud management compliance report |
| Mobile devices — corporate-owned | MDM enrollment with full management profile | MDM policy enforcement | MDM compliance evaluation |
| Mobile devices — BYOD | MDM enrollment with work profile only | MDM work profile policy | Work profile compliance evaluation |
| Virtual desktops (non-persistent VDI) | Golden image compliance; session-based agents | Image hardening + session policy | Image compliance verification |
| Servers | Management agent enrollment | Management agent policy | Management agent compliance report |
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-UEM-RAD-3.4.03.md#certificate-provisioning-integration]

### Certificate Provisioning Integration

Managed device identity certificates are provisioned through the UEM enrollment process:

1. Device initiates enrollment with UEM platform
2. UEM validates device eligibility (not in decommissioned state, authorized device type)
3. UEM requests device certificate from enterprise PKI on behalf of device
4. Certificate is provisioned to device managed certificate store
5. Certificate thumbprint is registered in asset inventory record
6. Device certificate is used as the primary identity assertion for Zero Trust device trust evaluation

[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-UEM-RAD-3.4.03.md#baseline-hierarchy]

### Baseline Hierarchy

The configuration management architecture SHOULD support a hierarchical baseline model:

```
Enterprise Security Baseline (minimum requirements for all managed devices)
  └── Device Class Baseline (workstation vs. mobile vs. server)
        └── Business Unit Override (where operationally justified exceptions exist)
              └── Individual Device Exception (documented, time-bounded)
```

Lower-level baselines SHALL add specificity; they SHALL NOT reduce the security requirements established by higher-level baselines without explicit documented risk acceptance.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-UEM-RAD-3.4.03.md#compliance-state-reporting-flow]

### Compliance State Reporting Flow

Configuration compliance state SHALL flow from the UEM platform to the asset inventory on a continuous basis:

- UEM evaluates device compliance against applicable baseline policies
- Compliance score and individual check results are published to the asset inventory device record
- Asset inventory makes compliance data available to the Device Trust ABB for posture evaluation
- Device Trust ABB incorporates compliance state into the device trust tier evaluation

[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-UEM-RAD-3.4.03.md#pattern-1-cloud-native-uem]

### Pattern 1: Cloud-Native UEM

Single cloud-hosted UEM platform manages all device populations: corporate endpoints via cloud-joined management agent, mobile devices via MDM, and VDI via image policy. All policy management, compliance reporting, and device identity operations are cloud-based. Most suitable for organizations that have moved away from on-premises domain infrastructure.
page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-UEM-RAD-3.4.03.md#pattern-2-co-managed-hybrid-uem]

### Pattern 2: Co-Managed Hybrid UEM

On-premises management platform handles domain-joined corporate endpoints; cloud UEM handles mobile, remote, and BYOD devices. A co-management bridge synchronizes policy and compliance data between the two planes. Suitable for organizations in a multi-year transition from on-premises to cloud management infrastructure.
page_texts.17:
[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-UEM-RAD-3.4.03.md#pattern-3-uem-as-security-agent-deployment-orchestrator]

### Pattern 3: UEM as Security Agent Deployment Orchestrator

In addition to configuration management, the UEM platform serves as the deployment orchestration mechanism for security agents (EPP, EDR, telemetry). Security agent deployment is managed as a UEM application deployment, ensuring complete coverage across all enrolled devices. Agent health status reported to UEM is correlated with the asset inventory for coverage gap detection.

[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-UEM-RAD-3.4.03.md#constraints-and-exceptions]

## Constraints and Exceptions

- Devices that cannot enroll in UEM management (e.g., legacy hardware without supported management agent, OT devices) SHALL be documented as exceptions, assessed for risk, and treated as unmanaged or managed through compensating controls (network isolation, dedicated monitoring).
- BYOD enrollment relies on user cooperation and privacy-respecting policies. The architecture SHOULD use work profile containerization rather than full device management profiles for BYOD to maintain user trust in the program and reduce privacy friction.
- VDI environments with non-persistent desktops require a different compliance verification model — compliance is verified at image build time, not continuously during sessions. Supplementary session-level security monitoring SHOULD be implemented.
